One of the major industry narratives at this year’s San Sebastián Festival, running Sept. 18-26, will be the presentation of SETT, the venture capital fund of Spain’s Ministry for Digital Transformation.
SETT director general Javier Ponce and its audiovisual director María Coronado deliver a practical guide to Spain’s governmental investment drive powering up companies in Spain: What it’s doing, why, and where it could go in the future. The companies it s investing in – with more to be revealed – are likely to be among the most dynamic in Spain.
What, explained very briefly, are the objectives of SETT’s Spain Audiovisual Hub strategy?
Javier Ponce: SETT is a public investment entity that manages investments in strategic, transformative sectors, including the audiovisual industry. It serves as a public catalyst for growth, employment, innovation and talent—all core elements of the audiovisual sector. SETT has managed the Spain Audiovisual Hub Fund, an instrument established under Spain’s Recovery Plan and financed through the European Union’s Next Generation funds.
Through the Spain Audiovisual Hub Plan, SETT provides financing and equity or quasi-equity investments, either directly to companies in the sector or through financial intermediaries active in the audiovisual industry. The objective has been to attract private investment and improve access to finance for projects related to films, television, animation, multimedia and interactive content, among others. Priority has been given to high-impact projects focused on creating audiovisual content and intellectual property rights while ensuring that those rights remain with the production companies.
And the rationale of a sovereign venture capital fund’s co-investment model?
Ponce: It is based on public-private collaboration to launch transformative initiatives that, because of their innovative nature, involve additional risks that make it difficult to attract purely private funding. Only highly liquid, large-scale markets with a long-established audiovisual industry are able to mobilize sufficient capital to finance major new productions or transformative industry initiatives.
SETT’s Spain AVS Hub fund could draw down up to €1.5 billion ($1.75 billion) from NextGeneration E.U. funding. According to María Gonzalez Veracruz, investments made are just under €250 million. Her explanation is that you simply ran out of time. Could you comment?
Ponce: Indeed, European funds have been fundamental for Spain, and the Recovery Plan has played a key role in driving major structural reforms and stimulating economic growth. However, it is also true that these funds came with specific requirements, including strict implementation deadlines, which made optimal execution more challenging.
For the audiovisual sector, the possibility of co-investing alongside a public entity represented a major innovation. Time therefore became a critical factor, as market participants first needed to understand the role and implications of partnering with a public investor that shared both risks and returns.
The next challenge is to ensure that these investments continue to thrive, identify new opportunities, and maintain confidence in the talent and ambition of Spanish audiovisual companies, which now benefit from SETT’s backing.
SETT, however, is not over, I believe. Obviously it has to exercise governance over investment accords now struck. I believe as well that there are plans to launch a new program España Crece, with a €13.3 billion ($15.6 billion) budget, held by ICO, but whose investments will be handled in part by SETT, if I understand correctly. Could you comment?
Ponce: The audiovisual sector will remain one of SETT’s strategic areas of activity and will continue under new fund “España Crece”. We have begun discussions with ICO to define the procedures and framework for collaboration between the two institutions, ensuring the continuation of co-investment in strategic technologies and sectors.
SETT has represented a significant shift in the way public investment in strategic industries is conceived. Through SETT, the State acts as a catalyst and partner in the most innovative areas of the economy, with the objective of positioning Spain at the forefront of transformative industries. That is why we invested in the audiovisual sector and why we will continue to do so.
Its ability to generate industrial activity, employment and broad economic impact makes it a strategic sector that will continue to enjoy our support.
Could you illustrate the rationale of SETT’s co-investment model in one or two of the investments made and the obvious benefits it could bring to the companies Spain’s film-TV industry.
Coronado: The SETT model has been built on three pillars. First, it adopts an industry-wide approach, rather than a project-based one, addressing the entire audiovisual business ecosystem. Second, its investment facilities are directed at the equity capital of companies or regulated investment vehicles. Third, it promotes public-private partnership instruments on a medium-long term.
Under this model, promoters must convince a genuinely private investor that their company represents a worthwhile investment opportunity. SETT co-invests alongside the private investor on a pari passu basis: public investment is intended to support companies, but always under the same terms and conditions as private capital.
This approach strengthens both domestic and international private investment in companies based in Spain, while also attracting foreign businesses that see Spain as an attractive location to establish their operations. Clear examples include the South African transactions involving The Refinery and Moonlighting, with a combined investment of €25 million, as well as Amuse Labs and Milo, two leading examples of Spain’s animation industry, which have mobilised €13 million and €19 million respectively.
My sense is that SETT investors can indeed help companies scale, create more such expertise and build infrastructure. But would you agree?
Coronado: In my view, the main challenge for the coming years is to consolidate the model we have been promoting and supporting. It is essential to continue strengthening and diversifying support policies so that Spain can establish itself as a global hub for the audiovisual industry over the long term. This means supporting every segment of the industry according to its specific needs.
Scale is undoubtedly part of the challenge, as is ensuring the availability of the infrastructure needed to accommodate medium- and large-scale productions, strengthening technical training, and fostering talent across the industry. It will also be important to continue enhancing the tax framework and the legal and regulatory environment to maintain Spain’s competitiveness, while further developing public-private investment instruments.
In addition, it will be essential to understand the cash-flow financing needs of projects to address the full range of companies’ financing requirements. Finally, the industry’s ability to adapt and diversify will remain critical, both in terms of technology and creativity, as well as business models and corporate structures.
In your view, does the introduction of sovereign venture capital in the Spanish film and TV industry encourage a change of mindset in the industry?
Coronado: Yes, absolutely. It creates new opportunities. It is essential to think in terms of medium- and long-term business strategy, rather than focusing only on immediate projects. It enables companies to strengthen their capital base, making them more ambitious, better able to protect their intellectual property, diversify, expand internationally, and bring their products to market more effectively.
What have you learnt in the two years of the Spain AVS Hub Phase II which you would like to apply in future investments by SETT under España Crece?
Coronado: The main learning here is the confirmation that SETT has a clear and necessary purpose for the industry, both in attracting private investment and foreign companies, and in creating opportunities for the local industry. It is important to allow more time for business plans to mature and for companies to secure private investment.
Can you outline very briefly what the SETT event at San Sebastián Festival will consist of?
Coronado: As you would expect, we will have a strong presence at the festival, with a wide range of activities. On Sept. 20, the Secretary of State for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence, through the Ministry for Digital Transformation and the Civil Service, which is leading the Government’s Spain Audiovisual Hub Plan, will host an event in which SETT will present the huge progress we have made in financing the audiovisual sector and new ongoing projects. Additionally, on 22 September, I will take part in a panel discussion at the conference organised by the CAA as part of Spanish Screenings Investment & Tech. That same day, we will also host an exclusive roundtable with investment funds and banks specialising in the audiovisual sector, bringing together both international and Spanish participants. We also have a few more surprises in store, which we will unveil throughout this very important festival for the industry.

Wembley welcomes 'rabid' college football fans
- Published
It wasn't even gameday in London but the rivalry had already begun.
Fans of the Kansas Jayhawks and Arizona State Sun Devils gathered at a pre-game party in Waterloo on Friday.
Kansas fans shouted their rallying cry "Rock Chalk, Jayhawk", while their rivals replied with "ASU, ASU".
After hosting 42 NFL games since 2007, this was London's introduction to a different kind of American football and a different kind of fandom.
Wembley hosted its first American college football game on Saturday, with 46,523 fans attending the inaugural Union Jack Classic (UJC).
Battle of the marching bands
UJC organisers vowed to create an authentic college gameday in London, and they began with tailgate parties.
Fans enjoy food, drink and music for hours before the game, and they are far bigger for college games than in the NFL. One American fan told BBC Sport she prefers the tailgate to the game itself.
The main tailgate at Wembley opened at 10am - seven hours before kick-off - with Kansas City rapper Tech N9ne helping to entertain the crowd.
Arizona State alumni held their own party, with nearly 2,000 fans packed in, while ASU's marching band and cheerleaders performed on stage.
But the wildest party was on Wembley Way, where Fox Sports had an outdoor studio for its live pre-game show.
It was surrounded by fans and the Fox crew kept trying to stoke the rivalry, while the Kansas and ASU bands battled it out on Wembley Way and on the pitch before kick-off.
Why are college fans so passionate?
The pageantry and passion of college football is what makes it different. NFL fans often choose their team, whereas college teams tend to be passed down through families.
"You feel a loyalty to your lineage," said Kansas fan Hannah, who added that college football fans are not just fanatical but "rabid".
BBC Sport spoke to families at Wembley who have had multiple generations attend the same school and alumni who now live all over the US but travel thousands of miles to watch their alma mater.
Current ASU student Sophie said her family "bleeds maroon and gold". Her friend Amelia has ASU merchandise all over the house. She just got a car that's maroon too.
About 15,000 fans travelled from the US for Saturday's game - 9,000 rooting for ASU and 6,000 Kansas.
College games in the US rarely have away fans but, with both teams having a sizable contingent at Wembley, as well as playing at a neutral venue, some visitors said the atmosphere was like a play-off game.
Why UK fans are learning about college football
Fans from 35 countries bought tickets and, as with NFL games in London, they represented several teams, not just those playing.
Neutrals wore NFL jerseys and college jerseys, of bigger schools such as Oklahoma, Miami and Texas. There were even some British university jerseys.
More than 100 universities in the UK have American football teams, and UJC organisers targeted those players, partly because, as students, they often find college football more relatable than the NFL.
They formed partnerships with the British American Football Association, British Universities and Colleges Sport and the Jacksonville Jaguars to establish links with the grassroots game in the UK.
The UJC has helped to train more than 1,050 British coaches and referees this year, some of whom were at Saturday's game.
Cambridge University player Alex said it has been "cool" to learn the stories of Kansas and ASU and he would probably go to more college games in future "if they're teams we can rally behind".
Will there be another London game?
After planning for an attendance of 60,000, Wembley was about half full at 46,523, with some ticketholders moved to the bottom tier to keep the top tier empty.
Although there were some big plays, the game was not as entertaining as anticipated as ASU claimed a 24-17 win that flattered Kansas.
Music acts played throughout the game and there was a light show in the third quarter. It gave UK fans a flavour of college football, but it lacked the pomp and circumstance of regular games in the US.
There were fewer band members and cheerleaders than normal, and the crowd was not as loud as during ASU home games – they averaged 54,000 last season.
Both teams took 105 players (or student-athletes), 90% of which did not have a passport before this trip.
Many fans and members of the coaches' families also visited London for the first time, and ASU head coach Kenny Dillingham said they had "an experience they will remember for the rest of their lives".
Kansas head coach Lance Leipold added that the hospitality was outstanding, while the hotel and practice facility "was a win".
Both teams are part of the Big 12 Conference, whose commissioner Brett Yormark said: "It exceeded my expectations, from the crowd to the logistics to how the local community has embraced us. It's been fantastic, so we want more."
UJC organisers have signed an exclusive multi-year deal with Wembley, and Yormark says other Big 12 colleges are interested in playing in London.
Big 12 teams also played two games in Dublin over the past 13 months, and the conference could expand to another international market.
Yormark said: "There's not a two-week period where I don't get a call to say 'take some of your product to this country or that country', so we're exploring that right now."
He said there will be an announcement about next year's London game "within the next month or two".
That will give UK fans plenty of time to swot up on the next two teams who will make their presence known across the pond.

Google’s AI models may not be in the lead by most measures right now, but the company does have one key advantage: your data. If you’re deep in the Google ecosystem, Gemini models have a lot of context on you already. Google’s latest Google Labs experiment, known as CC, aims to expand that kind of customization to the whole family.
CC is an evolution of something that Google announced in 2025. The original CC eventually became Gemini’s Daily Brief, which churns through the data in your Google account to offer daily action items and suggestions. The new CC has a similar goal, but it’s designed to be a shared resource for up to six users in a family.
Google says that CC has its own Google account, allowing each family member to interact with it (or not) as they choose. For example, CC only sees emails from its connected users if they are explicitly shared. You can do that by designating certain addresses as always available to the agent—something like school scheduling emails. You can also send content to CC via email or Google Chat. The agent can even monitor a shared Google Drive folder, into which you can dump invitations, documents, and other content.
One of CC’s main functions is, unsurprisingly, a lot like Daily Brief. Each morning, all the registered users will get a shared “Your Day Ahead” email that pulls together the day’s events and updates on previous tasks. It can also add items to shared calendars, remind you about important tasks, and create documents based on your instructions that are accessible to all CC users.

Mbappe, Vini and Konate obscure Real's Ceuta message
- Published
Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Ibrahima Konate rolled up their pre-game T-shirts ahead of Real Madrid's match at Elche on Tuesday to obscure the message of support for the people of Ceuta.
Ceuta is a Spanish autonomous city on the North African coast, bordering Morocco and separated from mainland Spain by the Strait of Gibraltar.
Players from both sides walked on to the pitch at Elche's ground, Martinez Valero, wearing white T-shirts carrying the message "Todos somos caballas" – translated as "We are all Ceutans" – along with references to the Spanish autonomous city.
While most of the players wore the shirts fully, Mbappe, Vinicius and Konate had theirs rolled up to around chest height, obscuring some of the slogan.
Mbappe and Vinicius then removed their shirts before the pre-match handshake, while Konate kept his on for longer. Their team-mates and the Elche players continued to wear the shirts through the pre-match formalities.
This is not the first time Real Madrid have shown support for Ceuta. Before their Champions League meeting with Inter Milan at the Santiago Bernabeu on 8 September, supporters in the south stand displayed cards featuring the coat of arms of the autonomous city, while the rest of the stadium joined the tribute with a round of applause.
The initiative was part of a wider show of support for Ceuta, following a major migration crisis in the Spanish territory after thousands of people entered from Morocco.
At least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July. Most swam around a border fence and at least 100 people died during the crossing, according to figures from Ceuta's mayor.
Although most returned, as many as 5,000 remain in makeshift camps or are sleeping on the city's streets and beaches, leading to unrest in the autonomous Spanish city in North Africa.
Locals have expressed safety concerns and some have destroyed shelters and blocked aid being supplied to the migrants.
The representatives of the players have been asked for comment.
The episode came shortly before a dramatic night for Real Madrid, who recovered from surrendering a two-goal lead to beat Elche 3-2, with Carlos Espi scoring the winner in stoppage time.
Mbappe was among Madrid's scorers, while Vinicius started the game.
The pre-match gesture also highlighted the differing approaches among players and clubs to the Ceuta campaign.
Barcelona did not take part in the initiative, while players at other La Liga fixtures had worn the shirts as intended.

Health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced Thursday a new effort to improve autism diagnoses, arguing that the current model is outdated, too time-intensive, and overreliant on professionals with limited availability.
“We are not satisfied simply for describing autism and managing its consequences. We are asking what drives the different forms of autism, and why developmental trajectories differ, why some children regress, and which interventions work for them,” Kennedy said during his keynote address at a conference for Children’s Health Defense, an anti-vaccine organization he previously led.
The initiative calls for organizations to submit “solutions” — tools and technologies that will not only speed up assessments but also improve autistic people’s quality of life. The program will be administered by the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, which funds novel health research. The announcement does not provide financial details for these grants.
“It’s exciting that ARPA-H is focusing on autism, and I think the idea of exploring ways that technology can transform aspects of diagnosis, interventions, and support is timely,” said Helen Tager-Flusberg, director of the Center for Autism Research Excellence at Boston University, in a text. “We can only hope that the review process will lead to an unbiased selection of projects!”
Autism care is facing some headwinds right now. Wait times to receive an assessment can stretch months or even years as prevalence has increased in recent decades. Health insurers have started pulling back from covering the main therapy used to treat kids after the field was rocked by allegations of fraud.
The autism community has also had to contend with Kennedy’s repeated use of dehumanizing language to describe the condition — he called autistic kids “damaged” during Thursday’s keynote — and his insistence that autism is correlated with vaccines, though there is no scientific evidence for the link. Kennedy and President Trump have also asserted, without evidence, that autism is connected with Tylenol use during pregnancy.
Many autism researchers have been wary of the federal investigations of autism launched by Kennedy, though they remain cautiously optimistic about the Autism Data Science Initiative, which awarded $50 million to 13 projects through the National Institutes of Health in June.
SPECTRA — or Systems for Phenotypic Evaluation, Clinical Trajectories, Response, and Agency — is a bet that greater understanding of interactions among genetic, environmental, microbiome, and other factors will provide advances in the field.
It will be overseen by ARPA-H Program Manager Russell Shilling, who has two kids with autism and used to sit on the Medical and Science Advisory Committee at the influential nonprofit Autism Speaks.

Hundreds of drones targeting Moscow and its surrounding region killed at least two people and damaged a major refinery on the final day of the country’s parliamentary elections, authorities said on Sunday.
The capital’s mayor said that more than 1,600 drones had been intercepted and shot down, 450 of which were aimed at Moscow.
Sergei Sobyanin accused Ukraine of attempting to interfere with a tightly controlled three-day election that is set to tighten president Vladimir Putin’s 26-year grip on power.
“The unprecedented attack was clearly planned with the aim of disrupting the elections. The enemy did not succeed,” he said on Telegram.
Moscow’s regional governor said at least two people were killed – a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man – in two separate locations.
A fire triggered by a drone crashing into a 21-storey building also led to 400 people being evacuated, said Moscow regional governor, Andrey Vorobyov, without specifying the drones’ origin.
The attacks come at a time when Kyiv stepped up its long-range drone strike campaign against Russia in recent months, particularly against energy infrastructure to target a vital source of the Kremlin’s revenue to fund its war effort – now in its fifth year.
Ukrainian strikes have knocked out a significant part of Russia’s oil refining capacity, triggering oil product shortages, fuel price increases and long queues at filling stations in many regions across the country’s 11 time zones.
A facility on the territory of the Moscow oil refinery had been damaged, Sobyanin said. No casualties had been reported so far and emergency services were on the scene.
That major refinery has already been hit by Ukrainian strikes in recent months.
Ukraine has not commented on the attacks. Both sides say they do not target civilians.
The latest strike comes after the US president, Donald Trump, said on Monday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed not to target each other’s energy facilities.
It also comes after Russians began voting on Friday in the country’s first parliamentary election since Moscow invaded Ukraine in February 2022.
Only parties that support Putin and the Kremlin’s military campaign have been registered to run. Moscow has also organised voting in occupied Ukraine.
Few Russians doubt Putin’s United Russia party will coast to victory again, but the vote offers a gauge of public support for the war.

Flock Safety announced a voluntary employee separation program on Friday, offering a “generous” severance package to those who want to leave amid growing backlash against the surveillance technology company, according to an internal email shared with WIRED.
Applications for Flock’s voluntary severance program opened Friday, and employees have until October 2 to decide whether to leave the company. Flock expects to grant buyouts to the majority of workers who apply, according to the email. People familiar with the program but not authorized to discuss it publicly say they believe that a significant number of the startup’s roughly 1,500 employees may try to depart.
Flock is making the severance offers as it continues to lose customers amid growing frustration across the US about its sprawling network of license plate readers, which have raised concerns about privacy and misuse. In the last month, WIRED has documented officers allegedly abusing Flock to track former romantic partners and colleagues, exposed how widely some agencies share access to the system, shown how little is known about the manufacturing of the devices, and revealed in new detail how much information Flock’s cameras collect based on data from a dismantled Flock device.

A wave of vandalism targeting its cameras has unexpectedly increased expenses. Without buyouts, Flock almost certainly would have to lay off some staff, one of the people believes.
In an internal announcement, Flock said the separation program provides “greater agency” for its workers and “treats employees with transparency, respect, and choice.” It also described the package as the “most generous” ever offered by the company, roughly double its previous severance offers.
Flock did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Some Flock employees have said they have received buyout offers in the range of tens of thousands of dollars, one of the people said. People familiar with Flock’s severance plan tell WIRED that some employees may take the offer amid speculation that the company, which has raised about $1.2 billion in venture capital, might resort to selling off parts or all of its business to stay afloat. “When you see enough of the vandalism” targeting Flock cameras this year, one of the people says, “you know the writing is the wall” that something has to change.
Flock CEO Garrett Langley said on the All-In podcast last month that “the biggest damage” caused by the backlash against the company had been “internal morale.”
“Because you go on to X or you go on to Reddit and you go, why are people so mad at us when we've been doing the same thing for nine years?” Langley said. “And why are they so mad at us for things we don't do? And we just want people to be safe.”
One advocacy group identified 93 city and county governments that cut ties with Flock in August alone. Overall in 2026, roughly three times as many local governments have dropped Flock compared to the previous five years.

Over 30 people across four states have been poisoned by bacterial toxins after getting intravenous (IV) drips at wellness clinics, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Food and Drug Administration.
The people had received IV drips containing glutathione, which is sold—without evidence—for purposes like detoxification, immune support, increased energy, and skin brightening. Glutathione is an antioxidant that’s found naturally in the body. It has been studied as a potential treatment for various ailments, but so far there is little to no evidence-backed use for the tripeptide; there are no FDA-approved glutathione products in the US.
Nevertheless, it’s commonly used as a supplement and promoted as having various benefits. It’s most often used in supplement pills, taken by mouth. But popular wellness clinics offering IV drips of vitamins and other supplements have also been offering glutathione. According to the CDC and FDA, the problem is that specialty drug makers, called compounding pharmacies, are making these IV drips using glutathione powders that are graded for dietary supplements taken orally. This grading is critically different from that of purified products graded for use in sterile injectable drugs.
In an announcement late last month, the FDA said it had learned that at least two compounding pharmacies had been doing this and that people were getting sick. At the time, the FDA had gotten reports of at least 30 sickened people.
Illnesses
The IV glutathione products involved appeared to be made from glutathione provided by Medisca Inc., headquartered in Plattsburgh, New York. “The glutathione was labeled as dietary supplement grade, which is not an appropriate ingredient to make injectable drugs,” the FDA said. Medisca told the FDA that it had informed its pharmacy customers not to use the product for injectable drugs.

US President Donald Trump said on Saturday (September 19) he will create an “AI Force” to oversee artificial intelligence and plans to appoint an AI “czar” in the near future, as his administration seeks to maintain US leadership in the rapidly developing technology.
Trump made the announcement in a lengthy post on Truth Social, comparing the proposed initiative with the Space Force, which he established during his first term. He did not provide details on the structure, membership or legal authority of the proposed AI Force.
Trump said his administration would not “hinder or stifle” the growth of the AI industry. Instead, he said the government would support and monitor the sector while using existing criminal and civil laws to address harmful activity.
“We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry,” Trump wrote.
He also said the AI initiative would focus on identifying what he described as “BAD” uses of artificial intelligence, arguing that existing legal systems could be used to address such conduct.
Trump described AI as the next “Industrial Revolution, or Internet”, saying he expected its economic impact to be even greater.
He claimed AI could eventually account for as much as 25% of US GDP, although he did not provide supporting data for that projection.
Trump also said the United States was currently leading China and other countries in AI and that he intended to maintain that position.
Trump said he would announce an AI czar “in the near future” to oversee the new initiative. He added that people with high intelligence should apply for the role.
The announcement did not identify a candidate or specify whether the AI czar would lead a new federal agency, coordinate existing agencies or serve in another capacity.
The announcement comes after Trump has repeatedly criticised calls for slowing AI development and concerns about the expansion of data centres.
Earlier this week, Trump dismissed what he described as a conspiracy against AI and data centres and argued that the United States should not impose measures that could slow the industry's growth. Reuters reported that he has previously rejected calls for additional federal AI regulations, saying strong presidential leadership was sufficient.
The announcement also comes as Washington and Beijing prepare to discuss AI during upcoming high-level talks.
US and Chinese officials view artificial intelligence as strategically important to their economic and military competitiveness. The two countries remain divided over advanced semiconductor access, technology transfer and how AI should be regulated.
Trump is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington on September 24, with AI expected to be among the issues discussed in the broader US-China relationship.
Trump has so far provided few details about what the proposed AI Force would actually do.
His reference to the Space Force suggests a formal government structure, but the administration has not yet explained whether the AI Force would be a new agency, an interagency task force or another type of federal initiative. The White House had not issued further details.

The southwest monsoon has begun withdrawing from parts of northwest India, with the withdrawal line moving across western Rajasthan and adjoining areas, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Sunday. As of 20 September, the line of withdrawal passes through Ramgarh, Mohangarh, Phalodi and Khajuwala. The development marks the onset of the annual retreat of the southwest monsoon, which typically begins from western Rajasthan in September. The withdrawal process is expected to progress gradually towards other parts of northwest and central India, depending on rainfall and atmospheric conditions, the weather office said. The southwest monsoon typically starts withdrawing from the North-West in September, with its retreat progressing gradually towards the South and the East. The development will be closely watched as the monsoon accounts for about 70% of India's annual rainfall, and its withdrawal marks the transition towards the post-monsoon season. Meanwhile, the IMD in its latest forecast also stated that rainfall is likely to remain active across several parts of the country over the coming week, with widespread showers forecast over parts of eastern, central and southern India. In eastern India, widespread rainfall is likely over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Gangetic West Bengal during 21-26 September, while Odisha, Jharkhand and Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim are expected to receive widespread rain from 22-26 September. Bihar may see widespread rainfall during 24-26 September. Central India is also likely to witness significant rainfall, with Chhattisgarh forecast to receive widespread showers throughout 21-26 September. Vidarbha is likely to see widespread rainfall during 21-26 September, while east Madhya Pradesh is expected to receive rain during 23-26 September. In southern India, widespread rainfall is forecast over Kerala, coastal Karnataka, and parts of Karnataka during the week, while Telangana and coastal Andhra Pradesh are likely to receive rain at different times. The North-East is also expected to see widespread rainfall and thunderstorms over Assam, Meghalaya and parts of the region during 21-25 September. In northwest India, east Uttar Pradesh may receive widespread rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning on 25-26 September, while isolated rain is likely over other parts of the region. The southwest monsoon season has so far brought cumulative rainfall of 695.6 mm during 1 June-19 September, 15% below the normal of 817.2 mm. Meanwhile, heavy rainfall lashed several parts of India in the 24 hours ended 8.30am on Sunday, with Telangana, Rayalaseema and Tamil Nadu recording very heavy rainfall, the IMD said. Rainfall of 12-20 cm was recorded at isolated places across the three regions. Heavy rainfall of 7-11 cm was also recorded in parts of Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Chhattisgarh, Assam, Nagaland and south interior Karnataka, according to the weather agency. In New Orleans, an empty building becomes a free store — and roller skating rink
New Orleans — Scars from Hurricane Katrina are still visible in the Lower Ninth Ward more than 20 years later: empty lots where people never rebuilt their homes and boarded up storefronts where businesses never came back.
On one corner, an old Family Dollar store stands covered in graffiti. It looks abandoned. But twice a week people line up outside, and when the doors open, they rush in to find racks full of clothing and shelves piled high with household goods, toys, food, books — even packs of birth control. Mattresses and furniture line the walls and there are bins full of purses and shoes.
And it's all free for the taking at the New Orleans Free Store, where Ernestine Lane is shopping with a friend from church. They're trying on boots and winter wear even though it's mid-August and pushing 100 degrees. "The problem is, we're not used to cold weather," says Lane, "so when it gets cold, you're naked."
In this heat, several industrial fans cool the space: there's no air conditioning in the 9,000 square foot building. Lane says people might be skeptical at first, because of how the free store looks from the street. "They see the graffiti on the outside of the building and it's a misconception. I say 'Go in, there's blessings in there, go in.'"
Inside, it's a treasure trove.
"People who are struggling don't just want the bare necessities," says Dan Bingler, founder of the Greater New Orleans Caring Collective, a local mutual-aid organization that runs the free store. "They want nice things, too, because they deserve nice things, too," he adds. "People want comfort. People want care. People want fun objects in their house just for the sake of those existing."
Bingler, who is 42-years-old, has a history degree and used to work as a server and bartender in fine dining restaurants. When he was sent home at the beginning of the Covid-19 pandemic, Bingler says he started organizing grocery deliveries to older folks in the community, meal delivery to families, and help with laundry for people who couldn't safely get to a laundromat. "It blew up locally," he says.
Then, when Hurricane Ida hit Louisiana in 2021, "that put us in a position to have kind of like a community resource center," Bingler says. "We had so many objects and things people had donated."
The parking lot outside the abandoned Family Dollar was already being used in a similar way, but Bingler made a deal with the owner of the property to use the building rent-free. He just has to pay the utilities. That way the property is kept up until the owner is ready to redevelop it in the future.
"It's just a crazy opportunity," Bingler says. "I don't think it's really been tapped." He thinks the idea could be replicated at empty storefronts around the country.
That was more than three years ago. On this day, Hilsa Rodriguez, a 37-year-old mom who lives nearby is shopping with her stepdaughters, Angela and Gloria Calix.
Angela, 8, says she likes the free store "a lot." She's picked out some animal-print hair clips for school, which she shows to her sister. Gloria, 9, is shopping for baggy jeans. "I like to look for shirts in the summer," she says. She shows off a small, furry vest and explains, "My stepmom is a babysitter. I thought I could be nice and give this to the baby." She's also picked up some towels in case she goes to the beach and flip flops that she's not sure will fit: "I have big feet," she adds.
As the two older girls dig through bins and happily run around with their shopping bags, their stepmom peruses the shelves with her 4-year-old, Galya. The free store "helps us a lot," says Rodriguez, who has six kids at home. "To have all the donations that they have here," she adds, "we're very grateful."
In addition to clothing and housewares, the New Orleans Free Store opens its doors for other services twice a week. "We do free STI testing," says Bingler, as well as "some food handouts and some basic medical care." Plus art classes, free punk shows and even roller skating. "Somehow the ground is just the perfect, polished concrete for it," Bingler says.
On a Wednesday night, the overhead lights are dimmed, the industrial fans are whirring and Chrishana Simon is gliding around the makeshift roller rink. "It just feels good when you're on the wheels and you skate and the floor feels nice," she says.
Simon is relatively new to roller skating. She learned by coming to the free store, where they have skates available to rent, but she already looks like a pro, wearing a furry trapper-style hat with headphones over it and gracefully crossing one foot over the other as she skates laps around the floor.
"It's a beautiful resource for the community," Simon says during a break. "I come to skate mostly… then they have the pole, right?" She's talking about a dance pole attached to a table, surrounded by some couches — another fun feature of the free store. "I definitely skate better than I pole dance," she laughs. Simon and Diana Ledet, who volunteers during free skate, practice some moves on the pole before grabbing hands and skating off together, talking and laughing.
The store operates with the help of several neighborhood ladies who volunteer their time. Phyllis Matthews, who goes by the name 
"Queen" is sorting newly donated clothing. The retired social worker says she does a little bit of everything. "I'm all over," she says. 
"I'm like an octopus." She's on a mission now to find a truck that the store can use to pick up large donated items. Matthews says there's much need in the Lower Ninth Ward.
Erin Sims agrees. She's setting up a hot dog stand behind a counter near the back door. "I raised three kids in the Lower Ninth Ward," she says, "and my momma raised me and four of my other siblings down in the Lower Ninth Ward. I've been here all my life."
The only time Sims left was during Hurricane Katrina. When the levees broke, her house was submerged. It took her a year and a half to rebuild, but she doesn't think the neighborhood ever fully recovered. "We still have a lot of abandoned places," Sims says. "You can't get groceries... Even to get medicines you have to go to the Walgreens or Walmart. There's nothing down in the Lower Ninth Ward for that."
"It's the number one food desert in Louisiana," adds Dan Bingler. It's a void he's trying to help fill in the community with the Greater New Orleans Caring Collective. Because, as he puts it, the next storm is coming. "When something happens again, number one is we're closer. We're more prepared," he says. "We'll be doing hurricane relief... and we'll be a shelter, if need be... Even if it's just skating with a generator," Bingler says, the New Orleans Free Store will be there.

The Arabic-language Al Jazeera and Turkish state-run Anadolu Agency, as well as Palestinian outlets Al-Resalah and Shehab News Agency, all reported the news of the airstrikes.
Some of these outlets shared the enhanced images without making note of the alterations, reporting the location of the incident as the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood of Gaza City, the date as Sept. 15 and the identity of the young victim as Muhammad al-Zinati (الل محمد الزيناتي), a boy described as "no more than 15 years old" who was reportedly walking from a Quran memorization circle. According to the outlets, the video shows him approaching the man lying on the ground, identified as Sharif Shadi Labd (شريف شادي لبد), who was injured by an Israeli airstrike moments earlier.
The Shehab article and that publication's Telegram feed host other videos of al-Zinati's death, including clips reportedly showing his body covered in blood at the scene of the airstrike, as well as several moments with his father crying over him (longer video).
Getty Images hosts photos of the purported father, identified as a relative in several of the pictures, crying over a body, possibly al-Zinati. Its caption and other images match the neighborhood and date. The media-licensing company credited the pictures to photographers Ahmed Younis and Saeed M. M. T. Jaras.
Some of Shehab's still-image content appear to feature AI editing, for example the overly smooth look of an image showing the two victims posing together, possibly created from two authentic photos. The Al Jazeera (Palestine) Facebook page also featured (archived) one of the enhanced images, as well as other video clips allegedly from the same scene.
Via Messenger, we contacted Al-Resalah (archived) and Al Jazeera (Palestine) (archived) to inquire about the altered images in their Facebook posts, as well as Shehab News Agency via X to ask about another enhanced image in one of its posts (archived) — mainly whether the images were edited with AI or reposted from elsewhere. Al-Resalah and Shehab are both affiliated with the militant and political group Hamas, according to The New York Times and BBC News. We will update this article if we receive further information.
We found some of the aforementioned reporting by using Google Translate to search for the victims' Arabic-language names, a research strategy that can display results that may not show up in an English-only search.

The world is bracing for a “super” El Niño, and its effects are already being felt in India, where the monsoon has brought less rain than average but more intense downpours.
Meteorologists predict that the current El Niño, which is developing over the Pacific, could be one of the strongest in living memory. India is likely to be heavily affected, particularly later in the monsoon, when El Niño’s influence tends to strengthen.
But, as Ligin Joseph of the University of Southampton explains in The Conversation, its effects on India’s monsoon are not straightforward. A previous study in Science found that El Niño tends to bring more extreme summer monsoon rainfall to India.
This year, the southern state of Kerala has felt the brunt of the building super El Niño, with about a fifth less rain than normal. Yet intense downpours in the first week of August triggered flash flooding and landslides, killing 26 people.
The super El Niño is expected to peak after India’s monsoon season, but Indians are already keeping an anxious eye on the skies, wondering where and when the next deluge may come.

Quick Answer
iOS 27 focuses on useful refinements, with better Liquid Glass controls, smarter Siri AI, natural-language Shortcuts, Safari web-change alerts, separate alarm volume, improved Photos tools, AirPods EQ, smarter password handling, and several everyday quality-of-life upgrades.
Apple has finally started rolling out iOS 27 to all eligible devices after testing it in beta for months. If you are reading this article, the update is already rolling out. If your iPhone supports it, you can go to Settings, General, Software Update, and update to the latest version.
iOS 27 isn’t a significant jump from what we have seen from iOS 18 to iOS 26. For those who are not aware, Apple has changed the version names to match the year. So instead of iOS 19, they moved it to iOS 26 to match the year 2026.
This year’s iOS 27 is more about refinement and fixing the issues that came along with iOS 26.
One of the biggest updates for most people, at least based on our insight, is the ability to refine the liquid glass design. Apple is now offering a separate setting to make your liquid glass look more frosted or transparent, and also allowing you to set different volumes for the alarms.
Plus, there is a new Siri and plenty of other Siri AI features, such as creating your own shortcuts using natural prompts. Let your password app fix compromised passwords, monitor website changes for free using Safari, and much more.
I have been testing iOS 27 for a few months now, testing its wide variety of features. In this guide, you will learn about the 27 best iOS 27 features that everybody should know and use for a better quality of life.
Table of Contents
Best iOS 27 Features You Should Know and Use
There are tens of new feature additions and improvements in iOS 27. However, not every new feature deserves your attention. There are a few features that really stood out for me and are genuinely useful in day-to-day life that everyone should be aware of. So here are my ten favorite picks before going to the comprehensive list of features.
Adjust Liquid Glass Design Transparency
It is evident that most people hated the new liquid glass design Apple introduced in iOS 26. Apple made the entire UI transparent overnight with a glossy effect, which made text hard to read and was resource-heavy.
Additionally, a few apps failed to adapt to this design perfectly, resulting in a bad user experience. However, Apple didn’t back off from the decision. Since the launch, Apple has continued to refine the liquid glass design to make it better and more usable.
In the latest iOS 27 update, Apple is offering a separate setting that lets you adjust the transparency of the liquid glass design. This setting is different from what we have covered in our TechPP videos, and here is how to use it.
Build Your Own Shortcuts Using Natural Prompts
Extensions and shortcuts are the two easiest ways to add missing features, whether it’s on your iPhone or in any browser. However, creating shortcuts isn’t always an easy task. It involves dealing with plenty of elements and actions, which can be hard for a casual user.
But that’s changing with iOS 27. The new Siri AI will now let you create a new shortcut based on simple, natural prompts. Now you can simply describe a shortcut using natural language, highlighting what it can do. For instance: A shortcut that automatically changes your iPhone wallpaper every morning or a shortcut that reminds you to drink water every two hours.
Since it uses AI behind the scenes, the possibilities are endless. You can describe whatever problem or feature you want to add through the shortcuts, and it will do it for you. However, the current implementation is not reliable for complex extensions. But it is a good start, and it will only get better in future versions.
I found using Claude or Codex to create iPhone shortcuts is the most reliable way, and it works much better for me than using Siri to create shortcuts, which often don’t get the desired results I wanted.
Let Your Password Apps Handle Your Compromised Passwords
When Apple first introduced the Passcodes app in iOS 18, it was super basic and missed a lot of the features found on other passcode management apps at the time. However, Apple continues to add new features, and the recent iOS 27 brings the ability to fix your compromised passwords automatically.
In simple words, if any of your passwords are compromised, your password app will automatically renew them into new passwords without you having to do it manually.
Password management apps are very good at finding your compromised passwords in data breaches. However, previously you had to manually visit every site and change the password yourself. But that’s going to change with iOS 27, where you can simply tap to auto-change the password, and it does it for you.
Monitor Any Web Changes in Real Time
This is my favorite addition to the Safari browser. Probably a feature that can kill many third-party apps. Apple has added a new Notify Me feature to the Safari web browser in iOS 27. It lets Siri AI monitor real-time changes on the website and notify you. Whether it’s an e-commerce price drop, real-time stock changes, or even a new article addition to any webpage, Safari can monitor it for you.
The best part is, you can describe what changes you want to get notified about in a natural prompt, and it does it for you. Also, there are no hard limits on how many trackers or websites you can track, and it lets you track changes every hour. Weekly, monthly, or even daily. The only requirement is that your device should support the Apple Intelligence feature.
Set Separate Volume for Your Alarms
Another feature that Apple should have introduced years ago is the ability to set custom volumes for your alarms in iOS 27. Previously, Apple used to have a single volume for all sounds, including alarms, calls, media, and notifications. In iOS 27, Apple is splitting that up, letting you set separate volume levels for alarms, media, and notifications.
One-Tap Access for Your Wi-Fi and Mobile Data Toggles
If you are someone who frequently adjusts the mobile and Wi-Fi toggles on your iPhone, iOS 27 is getting a very big, useful upgrade. Now, without needing to open the toggle or the entire panel, you can just individually turn your Wi-Fi toggle on and off directly from the toggle. It is enabled by default.
If you have customized it, you can just drag and drop the new network panel to get access to these features.
Auto-Paste Suggestions on Top of Your Keyboard
Another feature that Android users have enjoyed for years is now finally available on iPhone starting with iOS 27. Once you copy text or take a screenshot, the iOS keyboard now automatically suggests the recently copied clipboard text and images, which you can simply tap on and paste wherever you want.
Previously, it required you to long-press, select, and tap on the paste option to do that.
New Custom Equalizer for Your AirPods
Apple is rolling out a custom equalizer in the settings for AirPods. Now, iPhones with iOS 27 have a native AirPods equalizer in Settings to help you customize the audio output.
The new custom equalizer allows you to adjust lows, mids, and high frequencies separately. However, it is only available for devices running on H2 or later Pro devices, and for older devices, users need to rely on Apple’s Adaptive EQ.
Quickly View Photos Captured by You
One of the biggest downsides of iOS Photos is that the images captured from your iPhone are mixed with screenshots, memes, and other downloaded images saved from third-party apps. This makes it extremely hard for you to find the photos captured particularly from your iPhone. In iOS 27, Apple has added a new “Captured by Me” folder to the Photos app. It only shows the photos and videos taken with your iPhone camera, letting you easily find them.
Let Your Earbuds Automatically Pause When They Detect You Have Fallen Asleep
If you use AirPods, Apple has added another useful feature in iOS 27: your AirPods can automatically pause music, podcasts, or whatever you are listening to when they detect that you have fallen asleep.
Most apps these days offer sleep timers that automatically pause after a certain time. However, Apple’s implementation is more dynamic and doesn’t rely on a set time limit. Based on your movement, the AirPods automatically detect when you have fallen asleep and pause the music. This can be extra useful if you are someone like me who falls asleep, and it also eliminates the need for you to set a sleep timer every night.
The Phone App Automatically Shows Relevant Information While You Are on the Call
How many times have you searched for specific information during a call with a service agent? If your answer is often, then Apple has added a very useful feature for you.
With iOS 27, the Phone app on your iPhone now automatically shows relevant information when you are on a call in real time. These include your reservation numbers, order details, confirmation codes, and much more, which Apple can fetch from other Apple services. This eliminates the need for you to search through emails, messages, or other apps while speaking to customer support or during a business call.
Apple’s Mail App Is Now Better at Finding Information
If you use Apple Mail, it is getting a useful update. Starting with iOS 27, Apple says Mail search is upgraded to find more relevant information based on your search.
Now, instead of remembering the exact subject lines, names, or even words in your email, you can just use your natural tone and search for the exact information you want. Apple says the Mail app can now display more relevant information at the top of the search results, and it’s also smarter, as it can automatically identify the query and find the relevant information.
Now, You Can Set an Exact Expiry Time for Your Find My Sharing
If you use Apple’s Find My for location sharing, it is getting a useful update. You can select the exact time when your location sharing should stop. Previously, Apple only allowed you to share your location for an hour, until the end of the day, or until you manually turn it off.
But with iOS 27, Apple is giving you more flexibility, letting you choose a custom time. Now you can set a combination of days along with the hours to share your location. This also eliminates the need for you to manually remember to turn off location sharing if you have set it to indefinitely.
Now, You Can Turn Your Physical Cards Into Digital Passes
Apple Wallet app in iOS 27 lets you convert your physical cards into digital cards and store them in your Apple Wallet. Carrying a physical card can be a hassle, especially if you have multiple cards. It not only makes your wallet bulky, but also makes it hard to find the right one when you need it.
Moreover, there is a high chance that you can forget it, and it could get lost. Now, with the ability to convert your physical cards into digital ones, the Apple Wallet app eliminates all of these pain points. Plus, even if you want to carry a physical card, I would highly suggest converting it into a digital one, which can come in handy sometimes.
Improved AI Writing Tools Across the System
AI writing tools were the first Apple Intelligence features Apple introduced in iOS 18. However, Apple left them out and forgot to update them in iOS 26.
But in iOS 27, with the overall improvements in the AI features and getting close to what it has promised, Apple has also upgraded AI writing tools throughout the system.
Now, these writing tools are more advanced and improved. The best part of these AI writing tools is that they are integrated directly into the workflow.
So if you want to summarize, shorten, or fix spelling mistakes, you don’t need to switch apps. You can generate, rewrite, or correct text directly from your iPhone keyboard. Plus, Apple is also integrating these AI capabilities across the system, including Mail and the Notes app, letting you easily access them anywhere.
Easily Create Calendar Events Without Specific Details
Creating a calendar event requires you to fill in separate details for title, date, time, location, and other details. However, with iOS 27, Apple is making it easy for you to create or edit calendar events.
Now, without needing to fill everything manually, you can just create a calendar event using natural prompts.
For instance, you can ask Calendar to create a birthday event at 4 a.m. tomorrow, and it will do it for you. Calendar app can now understand details such as important keywords, dates (such as tomorrow at 4 PM), a person’s name, and other key details, and automatically create a calendar event. Plus, you can also edit using natural language.
Connect an iPhone Directly to Gym Equipment
If you own an iPhone and want to track your workout data, pairing it with an Apple Watch is the most sensible decision. However, it is expensive and can be overkill for users looking for basic fitness tracking features who don’t need distraction on their wrist.
However, the Apple Watch has this nifty feature where they connect to your gym equipment and receives live workout data, such as your speed, distance, pace, resistance, and the duration of your workout, which you can then measure and analyze in your Apple Health app.
If you do not own an Apple Watch or don’t want to carry it during your workout, Apple in iOS 27 has added the same GymKit functionality directly on your iPhone. So now your iPhone can directly connect to your compatible gym equipment and receive the live workout data. Plus, if you have an Acura Pro 3, you can also connect and track your real-time heart rate information.
Pause Location Sharing Without Disabling It Permanently
If you use Find My to share your location with others, iOS 27 is adding the ability to temporarily hide your location without permanently ending location sharing completely.
In previous versions, if you wanted to temporarily stop sharing your location, whether it’s because your iPhone battery is running out, or if you are planning a surprise, or if you don’t want to reveal your destination, you needed to permanently stop location sharing.
With iOS 27, you can temporarily hide your location from a person. The best part is that the person does not need to be removed, and you also do not need to remember to turn the location back on after the situation has ended.
New Improved Cleanup Tool for Your Photos
I personally hate AI photo editing features inside the Photos app. Recently, both Apple and Google have added several features that are designed to alter and convert your photos into AI-generated ones. However, one feature that I found very useful is the ability to remove unwanted people or objects from a photo directly in the Photos app without relying on third-party tools.
However, Apple’s initial version of the Clean Up Tool isn’t as great as expected. It struggled to remove unwanted distractions from an image. However, with iOS 27, Apple has significantly improved it. Now it’s on par with other clean-up tools that perfectly edit the image naturally, without leaving smudges or empty patches.
Automatically Organize Safari Tabs by Subject
With iOS 27, Apple’s Safari browser can now automatically organize tabs for you. Many other browsers have adopted this feature, but it took some time for Apple to implement it.
If you use the Safari browser and have many tabs open, you can enable the Auto-Organize feature so that it automatically organizes your tabs. This lets you easily find them or close all of them at once.
Generate Your Own Extensions for Safari
Similar to iOS Shortcuts, you can also generate your own extensions using natural prompts in Safari. If you have an Apple Intelligence-supported iPhone, you can just visit the extension tab and give it a natural prompt about what exact features the extension might have, and Apple Intelligence will create a fully working extension for you.
You can just use this extension for an individual web page, or for all the web pages in your Safari browser.
New Siri for Agentic Tasks
Apple is finally close to delivering the Siri it promised two years ago. With iOS 27, Apple is introducing the new Siri, called Siri AI, which is now better at answering your questions and also better at agentic tasks. Plus, it can now search across your Apple apps, including Mail, Messages, Photos, Notes, and all other supported apps, and get information for you.
You can create a reminder, edit a message, organize details, or complete another task. Plus, Siri can also have better context, which means it can remember the information that it gets from other apps. Although at its current stage it is not as advanced as Gemini or other intelligent or agentic AI tools, it is a good start for Apple to deliver what it promised.
It will only get better from now on. Plus, Siri is directly integrated into the system. You can activate it from any screen. Plus, it is free to use without any limitations, except for a few features that Apple might put behind a subscription paywall in the future.
New Wallpaper Extensions
If you customize your iPhone and set a new wallpaper often, this can come in handy. Apple is introducing a new wallpaper extension feature in iOS 27, which expands your wallpaper so it fits correctly based on your iPhone dimensions.
In most cases, if your iPhone wallpaper doesn’t match your iPhone screen dimensions, it can look blurry and pixelated. Plus, if you want to set it as a lock screen wallpaper, it can also affect the depth effect, making the overall wallpaper look blurry and clumsy.
With this new extension wallpaper, Apple now extends the wallpaper to perfectly fit your iPhone’s aspect ratio. The best part is it preserves the main subject and only generates the matching scenery at the image’s edges, so that the subject stays in the middle without being cut off.
Reply Inline to the Messages From Android Users
With the iOS 27 update, Apple is putting an end to another discussion of blue and green bubbles and Apple’s tactics to limit RCS messaging.
Apple iMessage now supports inline replies, where you can directly reply to a specific message sent from your Android friend. This is like a nested reply where you can long-press on any message and tap on Reply. Along with your reply, the other person’s message appears on top, making it easy for them to spot and understand.
New Siri Visual Intelligence
Siri is also now upgraded with better visual intelligence, and it is now live inside your camera app. Now you can spot objects inside your camera and ask Siri to describe them. This can be especially useful for visual intelligence tasks, such as translating the text from a photo, identifying a specific object or food, or extracting the details from a flyer.
Plus, the best part is that, since it is being done by Siri, you can also ask follow-up questions and even delegate tasks, such as adding the extracted information to your calendar or splitting and storing it in any app. Now, adjust your lock screen clock to make it look smaller.
This can be small, but useful for people who often customize their lock screen.
Apple is now letting you adjust the clock size on your iPhone lock screen. Now you can adjust the size of the lock screen clock even smaller. If you feel your clock is covering the important details of your wallpaper, or if you want it to take up less space, you can simply use the smaller clock feature to adjust its size and make it look smaller.
Organize Your Photos Better
While Apple’s Photos app search is smart enough to find the relevant image you are looking for using just natural prompts, Apple is also letting you add individual star ratings and keywords to the photos. Starting with iOS 27, you can rate the photos up to 5 stars and add keywords.
Photos app displays these details while you are browsing your media library, letting these photos stand out from the rest. This makes them easy to spot instead of manually comparing photos to find the best ones from your extensive media library.
Save Photos Directly From Videos
With iOS 27, Apple also introduced the ability to save any frame from a video. You can simply use the Save frame as a photo feature, and the video frame will be saved as a photo. You can save multiple frames as photos.
Here is how:
- Open the Photos app on your Phone
- Play any video and tap on the three-dot menu at the top
- From here, tap on the Save Video frame as a photo option
Get the Most Out of iOS 27
Those are the 27 best iOS 27 features that everyone should know and use.
Apple has officially started rolling out iOS 27. By the time we publish this post, the update is available for all eligible phones. You can update and test out these new features.
